messages.author: 263f1fc934267fff
messages.subject: Model averaging using DIC
parts:
Dear list,

I am rather new to INLA and Bayesian approach. I would like to perform
model averaging using the DIC provided by INLA. However, I was not
able to find any relevant ref suggesting that DIC was appropriate for
that. Spiegelhalter et al. (2002) wrote "Whether DIC can be justified
as a basis for model averaging remains open for investigation": I am
pretty sure that people have been working on this for the past 10
years...
I found "by chance" a paper in an ornithological journal (The Condor)
where they use DIC for averaging parameters (http://afrsweb.usda.gov/
sp2UserFiles/ad_hoc/12000000SpatialWorkshop/
12ThogmartinSupplCondor_2006.pdf). they only cite Burnham & Anderson
2nd edition book (where the DIC is not used for model averaging, or at
least I couldn't find it)... So I was wondering if anyone could point
me to a good ref for DIC model averaging (just to make sure that these
ornithologists didn't use DIC too "boldly").

Alex (another ornithologist...)

I havn't heard about model averaging using DIC, but if there is some
kind of justification of it, I would be curious to know. [ The DIC does
not have a proper justification itself, so I am not very optimistic. ]

There is one paper that came to mind, I think they use AIC (and not DIC)
in the same manner,

S.P. Brooks, N. Friel, and R. King. (2003). Classical model selection
via simulated annealing. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society,
Series B, vol. 65, part 2, 503-521.

Computationally, its straight forward, as you just need a 'weighting
with DIC' wrapper around various inla()-calls, and then use that mixture
of results to do your inference.

Alternatively, you can weight using the marginal likelihood if you use
proper and meaningful priors.
